title: Commitment bands for private deployments, accelerated upgrade options, and SQ readiness tracker
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and validate a three-axis packaging experiment for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that couples (1) commitment bands (annual committed GPU-hour or node-hour buckets + mid-term top-ups), (2) clearly tiered support entitlements, and (3) explicit upgrade cadence options with paid accelerated/hardening paths. This ticket coordinates PM, Legal, Security, Sales, and Engineering to produce contract language, security questionnaire (SQ) mappings, pricing experiments, and pilot agreements for 3–6 enterprise prospects.

Scope and hypotheses:
- Hypothesis 1: Introducing finer-grained commitment bands (e.g., 0-2,000; 2,001-8,000; 8,001+) with predictable unit pricing will increase average contract size by ~20% for customers needing predictable throughput.
- Hypothesis 2: Offering an "Accelerated Upgrade" add-on (automated security patching within 30 days + guaranteed rollback window) sold with a yearly credit allotment will reduce sales friction for regulated customers and drive incremental ARR.
- Hypothesis 3: Mapping Security Questionnaire (SQ) readiness lanes to support tiers (Standard/Enhanced/Priority/Platinum) and publishing a transparent SQ response playbook will shorten sales cycles by 15% for enterprise prospects.

Deliverables:
- Pricing grid for commitment bands and top-up mechanics (per GPU-hour equivalent), with worked examples for 3 customer archetypes.
- Draft contract clauses for upgrade cadence options and SLAs, reviewed by Legal.
- Support tier definitions tied to response/patching SLAs and SQ coverage matrix.
- SQ playbook and a fillable template to accelerate RFP responses.
- Pilot engagement plan + measurement plan (KPIs: ARR uplift, time-to-SQ-complete, churn risk delta).
acceptance_criteria: Commitment bands defined with unit economics model and example quotes for small/medium/large pilots
Legal-approved contract language for upgrade cadence, rollback windows, and upgrade credits
Support tier feature matrix published and mapped to SQ items in a playbook
Three pilot customers signed NDAs and commercial pilots scoped
Engineering has an agreed task list and estimate for automating accelerated upgrades and top-up telemetry
Sales enablement collateral (one-pager, pricing calculator, SQ checklist) produced and reviewed

notes: Trade-offs discussed: deeper commitment bands improve gross margin but add contract complexity—plan to pilot 3 bands and evaluate sales feedback before expanding.
Operational risk: increased upgrade velocity raises regression risk. Mitigation: canary rollout + automatic fallback + upgrade credits that fund 'accelerated rollback support' from Redwood SRE team.
Pricing nuance: offer mid-term top-ups priced at a small premium vs. upfront commit to preserve revenue predictability while giving customers flexibility.
Metrics to track during pilots: average contract value, time to complete SQ, number of upgrade incidents, customer satisfaction for upgrade window (CSAT), and churn intent signals.
